drills.q: Why can't you just do exact k-NN at scale?
drills.a: Exact k-NN is O(N*dim) per query -- every query touches every vector. Past a few hundred thousand vectors this blows interactive latency budgets and gets strictly worse as the corpus grows.

drills.q: What's the difference between efConstruction and efSearch, and which one requires a rebuild to change?
drills.a: efConstruction is the candidate list size at build time (affects recall baked into the graph, no query-time cost). efSearch is the query-time beam width (affects recall and latency per query). efConstruction requires a rebuild to change; efSearch is a runtime knob.

drills.q: Walk through the memory math for a 10M-vector HNSW index at 768 dimensions with M=16.
Explain IVF-PQ's nlist and nprobe, and product quantization's accuracy cost.
drills.a: nlist = number of k-means centroids partitioning the space (rule of thumb sqrt(N)); nprobe = cells searched per query, trading recall for latency directly. PQ quantizes each subspace against a small codebook, storing only the index -- this bakes in a quantization error at index time that no amount of nprobe tuning can fix.

drills.q: Why is filtered vector search harder than adding a WHERE clause to a normal query?
drills.a: ANN indexes (HNSW graph, IVF lists) are built assuming any indexed vector is a valid target. A filter restricts valid targets after the fact; pre-filtering can fall back to brute force over the filtered subset, and naive post-filtering can under-return on selective filters since the search never routed toward filter-valid graph regions.

drills.q: How does DiskANN achieve billion-scale search with limited RAM?
drills.a: Builds a single-layer Vamana graph via randomized init + two-pass robust pruning; keeps only PQ-compressed vectors in RAM for approximate first-pass distance estimates, while full vectors and graph adjacency live together on SSD so one disk read per hop returns both. Reports 5000+ QPS, <3ms mean latency, 95%+ recall@1 on SIFT1B with 16 cores/64GB RAM.

drills.q: A team wants 99%+ recall from an IVF-PQ index and can't get there no matter how they tune nprobe. What's going on and what do you tell them?
drills.a: The ceiling is quantization error, not search breadth -- nprobe controls how much of an already-lossy index you search, not the precision of what's stored. Fix: reduce PQ's compression (more subspaces/bits, trading back memory savings), or abandon PQ for flat/HNSW if recall is truly non-negotiable and the memory budget allows.

drills.q: Design a vector index strategy for a multi-tenant SaaS product sharing a 50M-vector corpus where tenant sizes range from 100 to 5 million vectors.
drills.a: Filter selectivity varies by four orders of magnitude, making a filter-aware index (ACORN-style or filterable HNSW) close to mandatory since neither pure pre- nor post-filter serves both extremes well. For the smallest tenants, per-tenant physical partitioning (brute force over a few hundred vectors) may beat a shared filtered index. For the largest tenants, per-tenant HNSW indexes sidestep the filtered-search problem at the cost of more indexes to operate. Name both the filtered-search cost and the ops cost of physical partitioning explicitly.
